_comment: Templates that switch a page to each layout the package ships besides the default one, for developers and CI. A Proclaim template is its params blob, so each entry is a copy of the installed Default template's params with `params` merged over it (values as strings, the way the form saves them). A template is applied through a menu item, not a `t=` query parameter, which is ignored once a menu item matches; so each `pages` entry becomes a menu item (note `<marker>templates`) whose page build/verify-frontend.php fetches as a guest. `expect` is markup only that layout produces; `differsFromDefault` (default true) also asserts the same view under the Default template does not contain it. That cannot hold for `sermonstemplate = simple` while the site is in Simple Mode, which a fresh install is: Default renders the same layout then. `item` names a row from content.json (`teacher:<key>` or `series:<key>`) for views that show one. `undeclared` lists params no form declares, which a site can only have from old data or an import; every other key must be declared in admin/forms/template.xml, because the form drops undeclared keys on save. Every entry except `series-legacy-expert` is a state the template form produces. The teacher cards and list are sub-layouts the main teacher layout loads for Show Teacher Studies = Cards (3) or List (4), not alternatives to it: setting `teachertemplate` to either renders the sub-layout alone, a state no admin produces. `series-legacy-expert` carries the params of expert mode, retired in 9.0.0 and finished for series later: a site may still have them in its data, and its series pages must render the normal layout (the list one used to 500).
